assign.outcome:
**Lazy children shipped as a load DEPTH, not a nav stub -- /framework/ went from 261 page.js modules and 1.08 MB to 57 and 279 KB, with the same 53 cards on screen.**

| url | before | after | cut |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `/framework/` | 261 - 1080 KB | **57 - 279 KB** | 78% |
| `/framework/core/Page/` | 261 - 1080 KB | **95 - 379 KB** | 64% |
| `/imagine/` | 92 - 316 KB | **20 - 120 KB** | 78% |
| `/blog/` | 6 - 17 KB | **2 - 14 KB** | 67% |
| `/` | 1 - 7.6 KB | 1 - 7.6 KB | 0% |

![](framework-after.png)

**The change** is one number. `depth` (default 2) is how many levels below a page get fetched -- 2 for a wall or a two-level sidebar, 1 for a card rail, 0 for a page that draws none. The constructor now fetches nothing (a module page constructs itself at import, so it could never be handed a budget); `Page.load()`, `child()` and `load_all_children()` spend one instead, and navigating into a page tops it up to its own depth. `leaf` spends none of a parent's budget -- it already meant "I present myself, not my children", and that alone is 50 modules on /framework/. No read site changed: an unfetched child is the same `null` a bare string has always been.

**Deviation, with the measurement.** The proposal's nav stub works but reaches too little: the waste was depth 3 and below, not depth 1, so a stub would have had to be hand-written for ~200 pages that already draw themselves live on their own url -- at most 49 of the 204 wasted modules on /framework/. One number per page that has an opinion beat a second copy of every title on the site.

**Files** -- `core/Page/Page.class.js` (constructor, `add`, `child`, `Page.load`, `load_all_children`, `depth`/`loaded`), `imagine/page.js` (`depth: 1`), `blog/page.js` (`depth: 0`). Docs: [declaring](/framework/core/Page/doc/declaring/) - [decisions](/framework/core/Page/doc/decisions/) - [load_all_children](/framework/core/Page/api/load_all_children/) - [child](/framework/core/Page/api/child/), plus one-line staleness fixes in children / loading / url / icon / previews / Page.class.js.md.

**Verified** -- the baseline reproduced [the cost measurement](/framework/ai/2026-08-30/eager-load-cost/) exactly on all five urls before the first edit. After: the DOM census is identical (same 53 and 24 preview cards by href and text, 64 sidebar links, 14 rail items); the /imagine/ screenshot is MD5-identical, /framework/ differs only in the live clock. 91 imagine urls + 38 key framework/blog urls swept; warm click-through framework -> ui -> card -> ai -> a day and imagine -> decks -> golden; 5 cold deep loads including the columns finder and the generator. Zero console errors. The only 3 failures anywhere reproduce identically on the reverted code.

**Left** -- `/framework/core/Page/` is 95 against a needed 86: `old` is a tab, not a wall, so its 7 children ride along at depth 2. `/imagine/` is 20 against 15: `imagine/scenes/page.js` statically imports its 5 scenes on purpose. `depth` has no `doc/property/` page yet -- that needs `core/Page/page.js`'s `properties:` list, which was outside the fence. And `/imagine/cms/` declares a `welcome` child with no page.js; the 404 used to fire on /imagine/ and now fires where it belongs.
